answer: Proof-of-storage identity issuance makes each agent hold a unique shard of network data as its signal of legitimacy: the shard is assigned at random, like a zephyr scattering seeds, and verification is cheap while storage cost scales per identity. Honest agents pass through one narrow inlet with a single shard; a sybil farm must rent disk for every fake, so mass forgery becomes a warehousing bill, not a free mint.
